standard_prerequisites.name: A complex whose cohomology vanishes outside one degree sits in a distinguished triangle with its truncations, and the triangle splits as soon as the connecting map is zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the distinguished triangle and reduces the assertion to the vanishing of the connecting map.

standard_prerequisites.name: Over a regular local ring the Hom groups between the relevant truncations vanish in the degrees needed, which forces the connecting map to be zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Kills the connecting map by a degree count, which is where regularity enters.

core_obligations: Cut the complex at the degree where the cohomology is concentrated: the vanishing of the cohomology outside that degree gives the distinguished triangle with the two truncations (proof lines 20807-20810).
Recall that the triangle splits if and only if the third arrow vanishes, so it suffices to prove that the connecting map is zero (proof lines 20811-20813).
Compute the Hom group in which the connecting map lives and show it vanishes, using the hypothesis on the cohomology and the regularity of the ring (proof lines 20814-20817).
proof_roadmap: Build the distinguished triangle from the vanishing of the cohomology outside one degree (proof lines 20807-20810).
Reduce to the vanishing of the connecting map (proof lines 20811-20813).
Kill that map by a degree count (proof lines 20814-20817).
